name: Litho Purple
lede: Litho Purple is a dusty, grayed purple named from the Greek root for stone, one of a scattered set of color words built on *litho-*.

sections.title: A stone word
sections.body:
The library records Litho Purple as a 1912 Ridgway name, plate XXV, hue 63′, tone i, carried into the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 as block 223, moderate purple, and cited again by Maerz and Paul in 1930 [1][2]. Its root, *litho-*, is the Greek word for stone, the same root in lithography and lithium [1].

Which stone the namer had in mind is undocumented here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[dauphin-s-violet]] and [[haematoxylin-violet]], at Compare [[wisteria]] and [[mauve]] for other grayed purples [2]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[dusty-purple]], 4.8 ΔE away, purpler and duller [1]. Further out still, [[manganese-violet]] sits 4.3 ΔE away, more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a color within six units of this one in only 2, about 0.01 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest is Gervase Spencer's Portrait of a Lady (1760); the other is Paul Signac's Woman with a Parasol (1893) [3]. With so few matches, nothing here supports a claim about when or where the color was common [3]. The count is a screen-color match, not a pigment identification [3].
